title: Product Recommendation System
short_summary: A product recommendation system for furniture where users swipe through products or specify constraints in natural language. Concerns were raised regarding whether users would pay or only use it once, leading to a debate on monetizing via affiliate purchases. While Leonarda questioned building an affiliate business, Marko and Giacomo debated whether overthinking monetization is appropriate for a hackathon.
summary: The team discussed building an AI-powered furniture recommendation and placement system that allows users to find items using natural language queries. However, they struggled with scoping challenges, including data maintenance, accurate dimension rendering, and differentiation from existing tools like Google Shopping.

competitors.summary: Incumbents excel either at catalog scale or single-brand AR, leaving an opening for cross-brand conversational curation.

competitors.name: IKEA Kreativ
competitors.summary: An AI and spatial computing tool allowing customers to visualize catalog furniture in scanned rooms.
competitors.differentiator: Proprietary spatial scanning tied exclusively to IKEA's single-brand retail ecosystem.
competitors.idea: Virtual room design and furniture placement using spatial scanning and machine learning.
competitors.shortBio: IKEA's digital interior design platform developed from its acquisition of Geomagical Labs.
competitors.howWeDiffer: We aggregate cross-retailer inventory via natural language search rather than locking users into a single brand.

competitors.name: Collov AI
competitors.summary: A generative interior design platform that restyles room photos and links aesthetic styles to furniture purchases.
competitors.differentiator: Generative diffusion models applied directly to room images for instant visual restyling.
competitors.idea: AI-generated interior styling paired with multi-vendor product recommendations.
competitors.shortBio: A venture-backed startup offering generative interior design tools for consumers and real estate staging.
competitors.howWeDiffer: We focus on conversational dimension-aware search rather than purely aesthetic generative image re-skinning.

competitors.name: Google Shopping
competitors.summary: A global product search engine indexing millions of merchant listings with keyword and visual search.
competitors.differentiator: Unmatched crawling infrastructure and universal merchant reach across the web.
competitors.shortBio: Google's dedicated commercial search platform connecting consumers with distributed retail catalogs.
competitors.howWeDiffer: We evaluate spatial fit and interactive room context instead of returning disconnected tabular product grids.

competitors.market_landscape: The market bifurcates between closed single-retailer AR tools and broad search engines lacking spatial room context.
competitors.our_positioning: We combine cross-store conversational search with rapid visual placement to bridge product discovery and dimensional fit.

workflow.summary: The Product Recommendation System workflow captures user intent via natural language prompts or visual image uploads, processes the input through a recommendation engine querying the product catalog, and presents tailored furniture recommendations.
steps: Step 1: User provides input via a natural language text prompt or uploads an inspirational furniture image.
Step 2: The system processes the input using image recognition and natural language understanding models.
Step 3: The recommendation logic queries the product catalog database based on extracted features and intent.
Step 4: The system generates and displays a curated list of matching furniture items to the user.

workflow.image_prompt: A modern isometric 3D architectural illustration depicting an AI-powered furniture recommendation dashboard, with glowing holographic product catalogs, natural language text boxes, and visual image-matching nodes floating above a sleek workstation, vibrant and professional design.

pros_cons.summary: While offering high demo appeal, the furniture recommendation concept was deprioritized due to catalog maintenance, spatial accuracy challenges, and Google Shopping overlap.

pros.point: Interactive visual mockups of furnished rooms offer immediate demo clarity and strong audience engagement.
pros.source_context: Giacomo argued the visual furniture demo is much easier to show people than abstract text matching.

pros.point: Natural language queries solve genuine consumer frustration when searching for specific items meeting tight dimensional constraints.
pros.source_context: Alex noted buying furniture is annoying and Giacomo emphasized finding items matching natural spatial queries.

pros.point: Direct product referrals create an immediate affiliate revenue model monetizing completed purchases.
pros.source_context: Giacomo and Alex highlighted that monetizing product purchases through affiliate commerce is a valid business.

pros.point: Generative image shortcuts enable rapid prototyping without building complex 3D spatial rendering pipelines.
pros.source_context: Marko suggested using generative images rather than complex 3D rendering for an initial demo.

cons.point: Scraping and standardizing heterogeneous catalog schemas across third-party retailers requires unsustainable ongoing maintenance.
cons.source_context: Giacomo warned that third-party catalogs structure data differently, creating significant ingestion and maintenance overhead.

cons.point: Direct overlap with Google Shopping and Pinterest undermines defensible competitive positioning.
cons.source_context: Leonarda and Giacomo worried the conversational search duplicate existing capabilities of Google Shopping.

cons.point: Generative visual shortcuts fail to guarantee physical dimension accuracy essential for furniture placement.
cons.source_context: Giacomo pointed out that image generation shortcuts fail to solve critical furniture sizing and fit constraints.

cons.point: Infrequent purchasing cycles lead to poor customer retention and one-off usage.
cons.source_context: Leonarda observed users would likely use the app once, purchase an item, and never return.

key_risks: Unsanctioned catalog web scraping risks automated IP blocking and potential terms-of-service legal challenges.
Presenting inaccurate dimensional fits in visual renders could prompt costly customer returns and reputational damage.
assumptions: Users strongly prefer natural language conversational search over existing faceted e-commerce filtering systems.
Retailers provide sufficiently detailed dimension and pricing metadata in scrapable formats for placement accuracy.
open_questions: How can spatial fit and dimensions be verified without building heavy 3D room-scanning infrastructure?
What core feature uniquely differentiates this tool from Google Shopping or Pinterest visual search?

systemGraph.summary: System architecture for a multimodal furniture recommendation platform supporting natural language constraint queries, visual room matching, automated catalog scraping, and virtual staging mockup generation.

nodes.label: Client Application
nodes.description: Web/Mobile frontend for text prompt entry, room photo uploads, product swiping, and staging preview.

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.description: Handles authentication, client requests, file upload routing, and session state.

nodes.label: Object Storage
nodes.description: Stores user-uploaded room photos, scraped product images, and generated staging renders.

nodes.label: LLM Query Parser
nodes.description: Extracts semantic style, hard budget constraints, dimensions, and category entities from natural language queries.

nodes.label: Multimodal Vision Service
nodes.description: Extracts visual style embeddings and room context/bounding anchors using CLIP and object detection models.

nodes.label: Hybrid Recommendation Engine
nodes.description: Coordinates candidate retrieval, combines vector similarities, and applies metadata filters (price, dimensions).

nodes.label: Vector Database
nodes.description: Stores multimodal text and image embeddings for fast ANN similarity retrieval.

nodes.label: Product Catalog Database
nodes.description: Relational database maintaining normalized product specifications, dimensions, pricing, and retailer URLs.

nodes.label: Scraper Task Queue
nodes.description: Distributes periodic scraping and catalog refresh jobs across retailer targets.

nodes.label: Catalog Ingestion Workers
nodes.description: Scrapes external furniture retailer websites (e.g., IKEA), standardizes specs, and generates embeddings.

nodes.label: Visual Staging Service
nodes.description: Generates mockup furniture placement previews using image inpainting and diffusion models.

edges.label: Submits prompts, photos, and swipe actions
